topIssues.title: op-reth: deposit contract-creation receipt `contractAddress` uses tx nonce (0) instead of deposit nonce
topIssues.author: asdv23
topIssues.body:
## Summary

For a deposit **contract-creation** transaction (`to == null`, `isCreation == true`), `eth_getTransactionReceipt` returns the wrong `contractAddress` whenever the deposit sender's L2 nonce is greater than 0.

## Component

`rust/op-reth/crates/rpc/src/eth/receipt.rs` (`OpReceiptBuilder`), via the generic `reth_rpc_eth_types::build_receipt`.

## Root cause

`build_receipt` derives the address as `from.create(tx.nonce())`. A deposit transaction's `nonce()` is hard-coded to `0` (op-alloy `TxDeposit::nonce()`), and the OP receipt builder does not override it. So the receipt reports `CREATE(from, 0)`, while the contract is actually deployed at `CREATE(from, depositNonce)` — the sender's real L2 nonce, captured during execution and stored on the receipt as `depositNonce`.

The `depositNonce` lives only as a **receipt field** (set during execution); it is never written back into the transaction's `nonce`, so the RPC derivation has no way to recover it without an explicit override.

## Expected (op-geth parity)

op-geth derives the deposit creation address from the deposit nonce, in both construction and `DeriveFields` (go-ethereum `core/types/receipt.go`):

```go
nonce := context.Tx.Nonce()
if context.Tx.IsDepositTx() && r.DepositNonce != nil {
    nonce = *r.DepositNonce
}
r.ContractAddress = crypto.CreateAddress(from, nonce)
```

## Reproduction (observed)

Same deposit contract-creation tx, two clients on the same chain:

| client  | `contractAddress`             | `depositNonce` |
|---------|-------------------------------|----------------|
| op-reth | `CREATE(from, 0)` (wrong)     | 35964          |
| op-geth | `CREATE(from, 35964)` (correct) | 35964        |

`eth_getCode(receipt.contractAddress)` returns the deployed runtime code only at the op-geth address; op-reth's address returns `0x`.

## Impact

- RPC-derived field only — no consensus, state-root, or persistence impact; the contract is correctly deployed.
- Only affects deposit + `isCreation` + sender L2 nonce > 0 (rare path), which is why it has gone unnoticed.

## Fix

PR #21449 overrides `contract_address` in `OpReceiptBuilder` using the deposit nonce already present on the receipt, mirroring op-geth.

topPRs.title: op-devstack,op-acceptance-tests: extract reusable SDM acceptance harness for external suites
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #21958 — review/merge that first.

Makes the SDM acceptance tests drivable from outside this repo, so
optimism-premium can boot its own sequencer binary against the same
fixtures instead of forking them.

- **New importable `sdmtest` package** — the `RethSystem` fixture
  (op-reth sequencer + verifier + batcher + funder on one Interop/SDM
  chain), the repeated-slot warming workload that drives PostExec (`0x7D`)
  txs, and the SDM opt-in / client-version RPC helpers. Non-test so
  out-of-tree suites can import it; the monorepo never depends on them.
- **Generic external-binary seam** — drops the hardcoded `op-reth-premium`
  kind/helper. A CLI-superset binary is selected per-node via
  `OpRethWithBinary` + `RUST_BINARY_PATH_<NAME>`, applied after the shared
  options so one node can take a flag its peers reject.
- **`OpRethWithoutProofsHistory`** — opts a single node out of proofs-history
  (some superset binaries reject `--proofs-history` in certain modes).
- **`DEVSTACK_MONOREPO_ROOT`** — lets an out-of-tree consumer point at a
  monorepo checkout for contract artifacts.
- Refactors the existing SDM tests onto the shared package; removes the
  redundant `helpers_test.go` and `premium_baseline_test.go`.

No change to in-repo coverage — the same tests run the same way against
stock op-reth. The seam is purely additive.

topPRs.title: docs: re-home the kept kona pages and retire the book mirror (A5 Rust dissolution, batch 2)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784185257434409)_

Tracks ethereum-optimism/solutions#993 (Option A per Matthew Cruz, 2026-07-23)

## What

**Before**: readers found a 49-page mirror of a dismantled book under the Rust tab. The kona book's production chain was deliberately removed (#19101, #19778, #21878), nothing regenerates these pages, and measured drift had set in (0.1 version pins, phantom examples, a dead RFC process, stale architecture claims).

**After**: the 16 pages worth keeping live with the docs that use them, re-verified against source; the other 33 redirect to the kona source tree, root policies, and specs.optimism.io. The Rust tab is down to the 8 pages batch 5 will handle (op-alloy 6, op-revm 1, rust/index).

## Keep (16, moved with a verify pass)

| Old (`/rust/kona/...`) | New |
| --- | --- |
| `node/design/{intro, derivation, engine, p2p, sequencer}` | `/node-operators/kona-node/design/**` (new "Design" subgroup in the Kona Node nav group) |
| `sdk/fpp-dev/{intro, env, targets, prologue, execution, epilogue}` | `/op-stack/fault-proofs/kona/fpp-dev/**` (new "Kona" subgroup in Fault Proofs) |
| `sdk/proof/{intro, stf, fpvm-backend, custom-backend, exec-ext}` | `/op-stack/fault-proofs/kona/proof/**` (same "Kona" subgroup) |

## Delete (33, redirected)

| Pages | Redirect destination |
| --- | --- |
| `intro/{overview, why, lore}`, `rfc/archived/{monorepo, umbrellas}`, `sdk/overview` | `rust/kona` tree on GitHub |
| `intro/contributing` | root `CONTRIBUTING.md` (canonical per #21878) |
| `glossary` | specs.optimism.io glossary |
| `rfc/active/intro` | ethereum-optimism/design-docs (the live design process) |
| `sdk/examples/*` (7) | `rust/kona/examples` tree (none of the 6 documented examples exist anymore) |
| `sdk/protocol/{intro, registry, interop, hardforks}` | their crate directories under `rust/kona/crates/protocol/**` |
| `sdk/protocol/derive/*` (4), `genesis/*` (3), `protocol/{intro, block-info, l2-block-info}` | their crate directories |
| `sdk/protocol/protocol/{frames, channels, batches}` | the matching specs.optimism.io/protocol/derivation.html sections (pure spec restatements) |

## Redirects

49 new entries (16 internal moves + 33 external), plus the existing `/rust/kona/sdk/fpp-dev/io` destination repointed to the new fpp-dev intro home (would have chained, caught by R3). No chains: verified mechanically.

## Verify-pass findings (drift fixed against `rust/kona` at develop)

The node/design pages had drifted well past the replan proposal's spot-check:

*   `RollupNodeService` no longer exists: the service is the `RollupNode` struct built via `RollupNodeBuilder`; the intro, sequencer, and engine pages now describe that shape, and the phantom Supervisor/Runtime actors were replaced with the real roster (derivation, engine + engine RPC, L1 watcher, network, sequencer, RPC).
*   The `NodeActor` trait is now a single `step` method; the old `build`/`start` associated-types listing is gone.
*   Engine task queue: priority is Seal > Build > Insert > Consolidate > Finalize; there is no standalone ForkchoiceUpdate task (`SynchronizeTask` runs inside the others). Task structs, `EngineState` fields, `EngineQueries` variants, and the setup/enqueue examples were re-derived from `kona-engine`, and the Engine API version table gains the V5 `getPayload` (Karst/Osaka) row.
*   `DerivationActor` now takes requests over one `DerivationActorRequest` channel and sends attributes through a `DerivationEngineClient`; struct listing, pipeline-construction snippet (six-arg `new_polled`/`new_indexed` incl. `L1ChainConfig` and dependency set), and `produce_next_attributes` signature updated.
*   `SequencerConfig` gained `l1_conf_delay`; the programmatic example now uses `RollupNodeBuilder::new` with `NodeMode` on `EngineConfig`.
*   FPVM targets: dropped `cannon-rs` (abandoned) and stated the build reality (`kona-std-fpvm` supports mips64 + riscv64, but the maintained reproducible prestate pipeline targets cannon only).
*   Proof SDK: `OracleL1ChainProvider` moved to `kona-proof` (link and snippet updated; `CommsClient` is `PreimageOracleClient + HintWriterClient`, not `HintReaderServer`); `EthereumDataSource::new_from_parts`, `PipelineBuilder...build_polled()`, and `StatelessL2Builder::new` (with receipt builder) replace removed APIs; `StatelessL2BlockExecutor` no longer exists.
*   Typo class: the execution page said the L1 head is fetched "in the epilogue" (it is the prologue), the epilogue page attributed its own directives to the prologue, and the prologue described the agreed output root as "latest finalized" and named a nonexistent `L2ChainConfig` (source: `RollupConfig` + `L1ChainConfig`).
*   Link hygiene: dead `rust/kona/CONTRIBUTING.md` refs repointed to root `CONTRIBUTING.md`, glossary links repointed to the specs, `docs.rs/kona-p2p` repointed to the `kona-disc` source, broken same-page anchors (`#-gossip` style) and two broken link defs (`/kona/...`) fixed.

No `last-reviewed` stamps: all 16 are ordinary explanation/how-to/reference pages, not curated artifacts per the curation policy.

## Inbound links repointed (9 files)

kona-node hub (x2 + design link), kona-client hub (fpp-dev intro), kona-host hub, `node-operators/kona-node/install/source` (overview + examples), `run/mechanics`, `run/sequencer`, `rust/index` (Kona card), `rust/op-revm/index`, and the broken `rust/kona/CONTRIBUTING.md` link in `rust/op-alloy/intro`. Links to deleted pages go to the best live equivalent (source tree or specs), not through redirects. Grep confirms zero live references to any of the 49 old paths outside redirect sources.

## Checks

*   Nav validator: OK (413 pages on disk, 412 distinct nav entries, 1 allowlisted orphan)
*   Redirect lint: OK (608 redirects, 18 grandfathered pre-existing violations, zero baseline growth; run with `DOCS_LINT_BASE_REF=afe51eaca`)
*   Link-policy lint with specs-mirror resolution: 0 findings, baseline stays empty
*   The Rust tab now contains exactly the 8 batch-5 pages

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] The 16 kept pages read correctly at their new homes (nav placement, cross-links)
- [ ] Verify-pass rewrites match `rust/kona` at develop (node service shape, engine task queue, proof SDK APIs)
- [ ] Redirect destinations for the 33 deleted pages are the right external targets
- [ ] Hub prose still reads correctly after the repoints

topPRs.title: op-proposer: create super-root ZK dispute games
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Teach op-proposer the ZKDisputeGame (game type 10) create path (closes #21414, first slice of #21463). The defend path (challenge detection, proof requests, prove/resolve) is out of scope and stays in #21463.

- **Parent selection.** `SelectZKParent` walks factory games newest to oldest with paged multicall reads and picks the first parent `ZKDisputeGame.initialize()` would accept. Challenged-but-undecided parents are legal parents; refusing to build on locally-invalid games is defend-path policy (#21463 / #21445).
- **extraData.** ZK proposals submit `create(10, superRootHash, parentIndex || superRootProof)`. The root claim is unchanged supernode output (`keccak256(superRootProof)`). A tick is skipped when the safe timestamp is not strictly beyond the starting sequence number, so an honest proposer can never hit the `initialize()` ordering revert.
- **Single decision point.** `proposalExtraData` is the only place the game-shape decision is made; non-ZK game types keep the exact previous encoding (locked by a unit test), and the proposal log now reports the bytes actually submitted.
- **gameargs.ParseZK** (inverse of `Pack`); the devstack `ZKGameImpl` hand parser is replaced with it.
- **Config.** Game type 10 joins `postInteropGameTypes`, requiring a super-root RPC
- **Devstack + acceptance.** ZK presets now start the production proposer with game type 10 (honoring `SkipHonestProposer`); the four existing lifecycle tests opt out to keep manual control. Three new acceptance tests drive the real binary.

## Test plan

- `go test ./op-proposer/...` and `go test ./op-challenger/game/fault/contracts/gameargs/...`: 11 `SelectZKParent` cases (including a cross-page walk), driver ZK branch tests, extraData goldens, ZK ABI added to the `HasProposedSince` compatibility table, `ParseZK` round trip.
- Acceptance (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs/zk`, verified locally): `TestProposerCreatesRootZKGame`, `TestProposerChainsSecondZKGameOnFirst`, `TestProposerCreatedGameResolvesDefenderWon` all pass: the real proposer creates a root game, chains a second on it with a strictly increasing sequence number, and the game resolves `DEFENDER_WINS` and anchors.
- Regression: the four pre-existing ZK lifecycle tests pass (now with the honest proposer explicitly disabled); `op-e2e/actions/proposer` passes (non-ZK create path unchanged end to end).

## Notes

- Tiny conflict with #21983 (challenger side) in `multichain_proofs.go` and the ZK acceptance setup; whichever lands second rebases. The merged ZK devstack branch should start both the challenger and the proposer. After #21983 lands, `TestProposerCreatedGameResolvesDefenderWon` should switch from manual `Resolve` to waiting on the honest challenger's resolution.

topPRs.title: op-challenger: migrate ZK dispute game actor to super roots
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
## Summary

`ZKDisputeGame` became a super-root game, but op-challenger's ZK actor still
validated single-chain output roots and compared them against what is now a
super-root hash — so it judged every valid proposal invalid and could not
operate the game. This migrates the actor to super roots and adds the missing
L1-sync gate.

- **Validate against the canonical super root.** Replace the single-chain
  `OutputAtBlock` lookup with `SuperRootAtTimestamp`. A proposal is valid exactly
  when the source node has a canonical super root at the proposal timestamp whose
  hash matches the claim. Require `--superroot-rpc` for the ZK game type (instead
  of `--rollup-rpc`), mirroring the SuperCannonKona super game, via a dedicated
  `ZKDisputeGameType` case in flag validation.
- **Treat a not-yet-safe timestamp as invalid.** The source node only returns
  super-root data (`resp.Data`) once the timestamp is safe, so its absence means
  the proposal was made too early to be backed by the canonical chain — the
  challenger challenges it.
- **Add an `l1Head` sync gate.** Skip the challenge decision until the source
  node has processed past the game's committed `l1Head`
  (`CurrentL1.Number <= l1Head` → `ErrNotInSync`), reusing the exact sentinel and
  gate the super game uses. This stops a node with a stale view from
  over-challenging a valid proposal. Resolution is intentionally not sync-gated
  (it reads only on-chain state).
- **Decide on canonicity alone.** A canonical, safe proposal is not challenged on
  the grounds that its supporting data landed on L1 after the game's `l1Head`
  (`VerifiedRequiredL1 > l1Head`); the challenger judges canonicity, not
  l1Head-provability. This is a deliberate divergence from the interactive super
  game, and keeps challenge decisions off the `VerifiedRequiredL1` / safe-head
  reverse index.
- **Acceptance tests.** Drive an honest challenger through the full ZK dispute
  game lifecycle against a live `ZKDisputeGame`, over both op-node and
  op-supernode super-root sources: valid → `DEFENDER_WINS`, mismatched root →
  `CHALLENGER_WINS`, not-yet-safe (future) timestamp → `CHALLENGER_WINS`,
  child-of-invalid-parent, credit claim.

## Scope

The challenger only challenges and resolves. Proving is the proposer's
responsibility (kona-sp1) and is out of scope here.

## Test plan

- `go test -race ./op-challenger/game/zk/...` — unit tests: sync-gate skip when
  behind `l1Head`, `Data == nil` → challenge (proposed too early), mismatched
  hash → challenge, and a guard that a canonical proposal with
  `VerifiedRequiredL1 > l1Head` is still accepted (canonicity-only decision).
- Acceptance tests (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs/zk`) drive an honest
  challenger through the lifecycle over op-node and op-supernode sources.
  Verified locally: a valid proposal is not over-challenged (`DEFENDER_WINS`), a
  mismatched-root proposal is challenged (`CHALLENGER_WINS`), and a proposal for
  a not-yet-safe timestamp is challenged on the absence of a canonical super root
  (`CHALLENGER_WINS`).
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt` clean.

Closes #21415.

topPRs.title: sdm: add configurable post-exec refund policy seam
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Makes the producer refund inspector configurable through the EVM factory while preserving existing public SDM behavior.

Without this, optimism-premium must either use the hardcoded public refund policy or fork the EVM/executor machinery; its own `sdm-policy` implementation cannot be cleanly installed.

Refund state is carried across subblocks and restored for rejected or failed candidates. Replay and verification remain unchanged and do not invoke the producer policy.
